questions.questionText: If two goods are substitutes (Such as tea or coffee), the cross elasticity between them is–
questions.questionTextEn: If two goods are substitutes (Such as tea or coffee), the cross elasticity between them is–
questions.explanation: Substitute goods are those goods which are used in place of each other like tea and coffee. When the price of one commodity increases, the demand for the other commodity increases and when the price of one commodity decreases, the demand for the other commodity decreases. The cross elasticity of demand between two substitute goods is positive. In other words, if X and Y are substitutes, then a decrease in the price of Y reduces the quantity demanded of X. Similarly, an increase in the price of Y increases the quantity demanded of X. gives In the diagram where quantity of commodity X tea is taken on X axis and quantity of commodity Y coffee is taken on Y axis. When the price of Y increases from OY to OY1, the quantity demanded of X increases from OX to OX1. Thus the demand curve sloping upwards from left to right indicates positive elasticity between the two goods. Note- The cross-elasticity between substitute goods is positive and the elasticity of demand is more elastic.
questions.explanationEn: Substitute goods are those goods which are used in place of each other like tea and coffee. When the price of one commodity increases, the demand for the other commodity increases and when the price of one commodity decreases, the demand for the other commodity decreases. questions.questionText: In the production process, the equilibrium point is , where -
questions.questionTextEn: In the production process, the equilibrium point is , where -
questions.explanation: In the production process the equilibrium point is where marginal cost = marginal revenue. Marginal revenue and marginal cost method is the method of interpretation of equilibrium of the firm. According to this method, when the additional revenue is greater than the additional cost, then the firm earns Profit. When marginal cost is equal to marginal revenue, It is the ideal production quantity of the firm, in which case the firm has maximum profit. Marginal Cost - When a firm has to spend extra on producing one additional unit, it is called marginal cost. Marginal Revenue - When a firm gets additional revenue by selling one additional unit, it is called marginal revenue.
